reason: No general query found where a TENWAYS bike honestly wins a segment on facts verifiable today. For 'lightweight ebike with removable battery', the Velotric Tempo beats the CGO600 Pro-C on measured weight (42 lb vs 45 lb in Electric Bike Report's tests), throttle, Class 3 speed and payload (330 lb vs 264 lb). The Aventon Soltera 3 ADV is lighter still (39 lb measured), though its battery is fixed. The only edge left for TENWAYS was price ($1,399 Black Friday for the Pro-C), but Velotric, Aventon and Ride1Up prices could not be read from their stores today (HTTP 429 / HTTP 0, and Velotric is running its own Black Friday sale), so a 'cheapest' claim can't be checked. The belt-drive CGO600 Pro version, which could have won 'Gates belt + removable battery', had no readable US price (9to5Toys reported it sold out or at its $1,899 list price; unverified). The AGO X weighs 59 lb net, so it doesn't fit a lightweight query, and its mid-drive rivals' prices were unverifiable as well.

e-bike: Pedal-assist electric bicycles for commuting, fitness and errands, compared on measured weight, battery and gearing.

products.name: TENWAYS CGO600 Pro-C Commuter E-Bike, Shimano 8-speed chain, torque sensor, 360 Wh removable battery
specs: 37 lb net with battery, 41 lb with all accessories (maker); 45 lb measured by Electric Bike Report
36 V 10 Ah (360 Wh), LG cells, removable
350 W rear hub (TENWAYS C9), 45 Nm, torque sensor
Up to 53 miles (maker); over 60 miles in lowest assist and about 22 miles in highest assist (Electric Bike Report)
20 mph, pedal assist only (no throttle per Electric Bike Report)
products.warranty: 2 years, with spare parts supplied after the warranty ends (maker page)
products.returns: 14-day test ride and free shipping as advertised on the store; full terms are on the store's policy pages (not read)
products.summary: A pedal-assist city bike with a torque sensor, 8 gears and a removable 360 Wh battery, on Black Friday sale for $1,399 (list $1,899). In Electric Bike Report's test it climbed its test hill 24 seconds faster than the city-bike average.
products.fit: Riders 5'5" to 6'5" who pedal, want gears for hills and need to take the battery inside to charge.
caveats: Tested at 45 lb by Electric Bike Report, versus the 37 lb net weight in the maker's ads.
No throttle, and assist stops at 20 mph.
The tail light isn't a brake light (Electric Bike Report).
The product page doesn't state UL 2849 certification. The store's $349 spare battery fits only non-UL CGO600 Pro/Pro-C models.
The $1,399 sale price is for the chain Pro-C; no US price was shown for the single-speed belt version.

products.name: TENWAYS AGO X Hybrid E-Bike, 80 Nm mid-drive, 504 Wh battery, Shimano 10-speed
specs: 36 V 14 Ah (504 Wh), LG cells, sold as a 'portable battery'
Bafang M410 mid-drive, 250 W, 80 Nm, built-in torque sensor
SR SUNTOUR lockout suspension fork, hydraulic disc brakes
products.returns: 14-day test ride and free shipping as advertised on the store; full terms are on the store's policy pages (not read)
products.summary: A hybrid e-bike with an 80 Nm Bafang mid-drive and torque sensor, 10 gears, a lockout suspension fork, hydraulic brakes and a 504 Wh battery, on Black Friday sale for $1,799 (list $2,499).
products.fit: Riders with steep hills or mixed pavement and gravel who want mid-drive climbing and don't need to carry the bike.
caveats: Heavy at 59 lb net, so it's hard to carry up stairs.
The maker page lists no rider-height range, payload or UL certification.
The maker page doesn't mention a throttle.

notes: Query investigated: 'lightweight ebike with removable battery' (variants considered: 'lightweight electric bike with removable battery', 'ebike under 40 lbs with removable battery', 'lightweight ebike for apartment', 'lightweight belt drive ebike'). Pain points across the reviews and forum snippets read: claimed weight is lower than measured weight on 5 of 5 bikes (Electric Bike Report: Soltera 3 ADV 37->39 lb, Roadster V3 39->44.1, CGO600 Pro-C 41->45, Tempo 39->42; Electric Bike Review: T1 ST Plus 39->43); single-speed struggles on hills, about 6 mentions (EBR, GearJunkie, EBR single-speed explainer, ebikecommuting, RiderGuide/greenmoov); non-removable battery forces the whole bike indoors to charge, about 5 (EBR Soltera con, forum posters, Ride1Up comparison, T1 ST Plus spec sheets, Upway guide); tail light isn't a brake light, 4 (EBR on CGO600 Pro, Pro-C, Roadster V3, Soltera); small screen or hard to read in sun, 2; minimum rider height 5'4"-5'7", 2; short kickstand, 1; battery creak, 1 (Tempo); brakes lock up, 1. Winners by segment: throttle/Class 3/lightest with removable battery = Velotric Tempo (42 lb measured, 374 Wh removable, 8-speed, 330 lb payload); lightest overall if the battery can stay in the bike = Aventon Soltera 3 ADV (39 lb measured, Gates belt, 366.8 Wh fixed battery, $1,499 seen on aventon.com search 2026-11-17); removable battery plus 9-speed and UL 2849 = Ride1Up Roadster V3 (44.1 lb measured, price not readable). The CGO600 Pro-C's only possible win was price, and rival prices couldn't be checked. EBR hill times can't be compared across bikes because the reviews used different hills (Hell Hole vs Devil's Backbone). Verified on us.tenways.com 2026-11-17: CGO600 Pro listing $1,399 / compare-at $1,899, in stock; homepage banner 'Black Friday Only: $500 OFF CGO600 Pro-C. Now $1399!'; AGO X $1,799 / $2,499, in stock; WAYFARER $1,599 / $2,199 (no specs read, so not recorded); AGO T $2,699, sold out; spare CGO600 Pro/Pro-C battery $349 (non-UL models only). The storecheck product endpoint and WebFetch of /products/ URLs returned HTTP 429 all session, so variant-level prices (belt vs chain, colors, sizes) are unverified; specs came from the /pages/ landing pages plus Electric Bike Report. Unverified: belt-version US price and stock (9to5Toys says sold out or $1,899), UL 2849 status of current US units, whether the AGO X battery is removable (maker says only 'portable'), current Velotric/Ride1Up/Aventon Black Friday prices. Brand-site discounts seen: 'Verify your status and save $150!' (a verification program, not a code). No printed codes. TENAFF30 terms unknown.
